pll1d18c1-d1e3477.summary: Asks whether, since the Spirit, through whom gifts are divided, is himself a gift, it should be granted that gifts are divided and given through the Gift.

pll1d18c1-d1e3480.summary: Answers that through the Gift, the Spirit, proper gifts are divided to each, while all the good have the Gift himself in common.
claims: Through the Gift proper gifts are divided to each.
All the good have the Spirit in common.

pll1d18c1-d1e3483.summary: Cites De Trinitate XV: through the Gift that is the Spirit, many gifts are divided among Christ's members; not each has all, but all have the Gift from which each receives his own, the Holy Spirit.
claims: Not every member has all gifts.
All members have the Holy Spirit, the Gift from whom the gifts come.

pl-l1d18c1.summary: Asks whether, since the Spirit through whom gifts are divided is himself the Gift, gifts are given through the Gift. Yes: with Augustine, through the Gift that is the Spirit, gifts proper to each are divided among Christ's members, while all the good have the Gift himself in common.
claims: Gifts are divided and given through the Gift, which is the Holy Spirit.
Individual members receive different gifts, but all the good have the Holy Spirit in common.
